one_liner: C++20 lexer that finds CommonJS named exports for Node's ESM import(); replaced cjs-module-lexer, making cold CJS imports about 21% faster.
what_it_does: merve statically scans CommonJS source text without running it. It reports the names a module exports and the specifiers it re-exports, each with a line number, following the cjs-module-lexer rules that Node uses to create named exports when ESM code imports a CJS file. The C++ API is std::optional<lexer_analysis> parse_commonjs(std::string_view). Names are std::variant<std::string, std::string_view>, and errors (including ESM syntax found in a CJS file) come from get_last_error() and get_last_error_location(). There is also a C API (merve_c.h) and a Rust crate (rust/); it is not a drop-in for the npm package's JS API.
how_it_is_fast: It is a hand-written single-pass scanner that does not backtrack. It keeps the structure of cjs-module-lexer's lexer.c: the same open-token and template stacks with STACK_DEPTH 2048, and the same star-export backtracking. Characters are classified with 256-entry lookup tables built by consteval lambdas. Export names are std::string_view slices of the source, and a std::string is allocated only when an escape must be decoded. With MERVE_USE_SIMDUTF, which Node enables, simdutf::find locates backslashes and simdutf converts UTF-32 to UTF-8. Inside Node, part of the measured gain comes from calling native C++ directly, where the old path ran JS that called a WebAssembly lexer that had to be initialised first.
when_to_use: Tools outside Node that must reproduce Node's CJS-to-ESM named-export detection, such as bundlers, resolvers, alternative runtimes or linters, written in C, C++ or Rust.
Bulk scans of npm packages to list CJS exports and re-exports with line numbers, where a native library is easier to embed than a JS or wasm module.
Runtimes where the cold-start cost of instantiating cjs-module-lexer's wasm matters, for example the first import() of a CJS dependency.
Flagging .js files that contain ESM syntax: it returns UNEXPECTED_ESM_IMPORT, UNEXPECTED_ESM_EXPORT or UNEXPECTED_ESM_IMPORT_META.
when_not_to_use: Untrusted or adversarial source until a nesting-depth bound is added: parentheses and braces nested more than 2048 deep overrun fixed-size stacks (see gotchas).

You need exports that the cjs-module-lexer rules miss: module.exports = { test: 5 } yields no exports (open issue #27, the same won't-fix behaviour as upstream), and import * namespaces lose exports whose names start with 'get' (open issue #49).
You need a general JavaScript tokenizer or parser: merve only recognises export patterns.
Pure-JS environments: the cjs-module-lexer npm package stays the portable option, and merve needs a native C++20 build.
You need lexer-only throughput numbers: none are published, and the repository has no benchmarks directory although CMake has a MERVE_BENCHMARKS option.

integration.form: static or shared lib (CMake target lexer::lexer) or source-drop (singleheader/merve.h and merve.cpp); Rust crate in rust/
integration.dependencies: none; simdutf optional (MERVE_USE_SIMDUTF, fetched with CPM when not found)
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS and Windows per the README; scalar portable code, with SIMD only through optional simdutf
integration.thread_safety: parse_commonjs keeps its state in a local CJSLexer, and the last-error state has been thread_local since 1.1.0, so separate threads can parse concurrently (read from parser.cpp; not otherwise documented). Results hold string_views into the caller's buffer.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: it follows cjs-module-lexer's detection rules and replaced it inside Node core, but the language and API differ (C++/C/Rust instead of a JS/wasm parse() function)

gotchas: No nesting-depth check on brackets: upstream cjs-module-lexer guards every push with pushOpenToken(), which raises a syntax error at STACK_DEPTH 2048 in lexer.c and throws 'Maximum nesting depth exceeded.' in lexer.js. merve's src/parser.cpp checks only template nesting (TEMPLATE_NEST_OVERFLOW). Its five openTokenDepth++ pushes (plain '(' and '{', import(, __interopRequireWildcard( and __export( or __exportStar( contexts), and the ++openTokenDepth in templateString(), write to std::array<..., 2048> members with no bound. More than 2048 nested parentheses or braces therefore writes out of bounds in the CJSLexer object, which is a local on the stack in parse_commonjs. Because openTokenDepth is uint16_t, the index can reach 65535, about 512 KB past openTokenPosStack_. Node runs this lexer on any CJS file that ESM code imports. This was found by reading the code at HEAD; it was not reproduced (no build), and the repository has no fuzz directory.

Benchmark harness: the warm row of nodejs/node benchmark/esm/import-cjs.js asserts deepStrictEqual(Object.keys(require(fixture)), Object.keys(result.default)). result.default is module.exports, which does not depend on the lexer, so the check does not validate the names merve detects; those appear on the namespace object itself. The cold row times a single import() that includes reading, compiling and evaluating typescript.js, plus the baseline's wasm initialisation.

Zero-copy names: for exports held as string_view (most plain identifiers), the source buffer must outlive the analysis, including through the C API, where the merve_analysis handle must also be freed with merve_free().

Released versions had memory-safety and correctness regressions: a heap-buffer-overflow read when require() is the first token (Node issue 62212, fixed in 1.2.1 by merve PR 41), a ToLocalChecked abort in Node's binding (fixed by node PR 63885), 'get' export names breaking later exports (fixed in 1.2.0), and Rust-binding unsoundness (issues #16 and #28, fixed in 1.1.x).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The catalogued siblings (flex, logos, simd-lexing, the Zig SIMD tokenizer, LRSTAR) are general lexer generators or language tokenizers. Pick merve only for the narrow job of detecting CommonJS exports with Node-compatible semantics, which none of them provide.
verified_claims_summary: In Node PR 61456, merve's own author ran Node's benchmark CI to compare a Node build using merve with one using cjs-module-lexer on benchmark/esm/import-cjs.js, which runs ESM import() of the 2000+-export typescript.js fixture. The cold single import was +26.83 % ops/s (+/-0.58 %) and ten warm imports were +11.95 % (+/-0.14 %), which is about 21 % and 11 % less time per import (derived from page data). No CPU, compiler or flags are given, and the timing is end to end, including file read, compile, evaluation and the baseline's wasm start-up, so lexer-only speed is not isolated.
status_note: The project is active (v1.2.2 released 2026-03-11, last commit 2026-04-17), Apache-2.0 OR MIT, and shipped in Node v24.14.0 LTS and v25.6.1. It is young, though: there have been several post-merge crash and wrong-export fixes, issue #49 is open, HEAD has no bracket-nesting bound (a possible stack out-of-bounds write on deeply nested input), and the only numbers come from a first-party end-to-end Node CI run whose warm-row assertion does not check the lexer's output.
